messages:
sara: Heads-up — started onboarding reranker v2 (arch tweak + PTQ pipeline) against our multilingual holdout (EN/ES/FR). Quick sanity numbers below, looking for quick hypotheses before deeper probes.

eval-bot: automated-eval report attached:
```
Baseline (fp16) - all: NDCG@10 0.432, MRR 0.321
PTQ int8 - all:  NDCG@10 0.410 (-5.1%), MRR 0.298 (-7.2%)
Per-lang:
  EN: ndcg 0.435 -> 0.428 (-1.6%)
  ES: ndcg 0.411 -> 0.382 (-7.1%)
  FR: ndcg 0.431 -> 0.373 (-13.4%)
```

sara: Oof FR drop is big. EN looks fine which suggests tokenizer/encoding or doc truncation issues on multi-byte languages.

priya: First question: are we using the same tokenization & doc-prep across langs? We sometimes lowercase/enforce ascii-normalization only for EN pipeline.

tom: I think the bring-up used the unified preprocess config (legacy) that does not do language-specific normalization. Also candidate-doc truncation is by bytes (max_bytes=16000) which hurts UTF-8 double-byte chars — you lose more chars for FR/ES.

liam: Good catch. I reproduced a mini case: a FR doc with long accented text gets truncated mid-sentence -> context loss. That would explain hit to ndcg.

priya: Suggestion: switch to token-based truncation or increase max_bytes for multi-lingual eval, and rerun PTQ eval. Also test lowercasing toggle.

sara: Agreed. Another possible axis: PTQ calibration set was EN-heavy (80% EN). PTQ per-layer scale might be biased. We should run per-lang calibration or stratified calibration.

eval-bot: quick experiment command suggestion:
```
# token truncation + per-lang calibrate
./eval_runner \
  --model rerank-v2-ptq8 \
  --cohort multilingual_holdout \
  --truncation-mode tokens --max-tokens 1024 \
  --calib-mode stratified --calib-samples 2000_per_lang \
  --norm-case true
```

tom: Also try PTQ with per-channel quant (if available) vs symmetric layerwise. We saw better stability for accented languages in earlier runs.

priya: Small diagnostic we can run quickly: take top 100 queries where FR ndcg dropped most and diff tokenization of query+candidate between fp16 and ptq pipelines (same preprocess). If tokenization differs, that's a bug.

sara: I'll run the token-truncation + stratified calibration experiment now (queue job) and drop the top-100 diff list here once done. If that doesn't close >50% of gap, we'll run a QAT micro-run for layers 0-6.

liam: FYI, embedding/rescore ordering sometimes changes with KV-cache alignment when we prune candidates early; ensure eval harness freezes candidate ordering.

priya: I'll add a small harness change to commit that forces stable candidate sampling (seeded) and logs candidate lengths in chars/tokens.

eval-bot: queued experiment id: rerank-v2-ml-ptq-175400-1. ETA ~45m.

sara: Action items: 1) tom/priya adjust truncation & harness (priya) 2) sara run stratified PTQ eval 3) liam confirm candidate ordering freeze. We'll reconvene in this thread when results are in :eyes:.

priya: Also adding 20 FR edge-case queries (long accents, emoji, mixed punctuation) to the holdout—should catch tokenization regressions early.

sara: Great. Thanks — will post eval-bot summary when job finishes.
